note: No design-only option is classified as implemented or as TRUST_ANCHOR_ESTABLISHED.

A.ineligibility: A same-user launcher repeats the demonstrated CreateFileW race. A different principal is not evidenced.

points.1_root_trust_anchor: The launcher's first directory open. That open is still a pathname lookup.
points.2_who_controls_the_anchor: Whichever user runs the launcher. A same-user launcher is controlled by the demonstrated attacker.
points.3_how_created: Not created. The design would call CreateFileW or an equivalent path open.
points.4_how_authenticated: Volume serial and file index after the open. Those identify the opened object only.
points.5_how_retained: The existing DirectoryHandle can retain a transferred handle. Transfer was not built.
points.6_child_directories: NtCreateFile FILE_CREATE relative to the parent handle. Reusable only after a good parent exists.
points.7_artifact_files: write_exclusive relative to the child handle.
points.8_artifact_verification: Existing handle-read wheel checks. They do not prove directory intent.
points.9_export: Files already reside on the host. Export does not cross a boundary.
points.10_export_destination: Another path open unless the consumer keeps the same handle.
points.11_receiver_provenance: A receiver that reopens by path does not inherit the producer's handle identity.
points.12_receiver_substitution: The G.14.8 pre-open swap applies to the receiver.
points.13_concurrent_modification: Post-open replacement was contained in tests. Pre-open replacement was not.
points.14_crashes: Not retested. A wrong handle cannot be repaired by crash cleanup.
points.15_cleanup: Do not delete the directory. The current helper does not. Deleting a substituted directory would be unsafe.
points.16_partial_artifacts: interrupted_write leaves the file. The directory is kept.
points.17_hostile_metadata: Synthetic checks only. No live index.
points.18_same_user: Not prevented. The launcher is in reach of the same user.
points.19_independently_verifiable: Post-open binding, junction rejection, and fail-closed close. Not the initial anchor.
points.20_assumption: Either the same user is benign, which is Option C, or a different principal exists, which was not shown.

B.ineligibility: ENVIRONMENT_SELECTION_REQUIRES_FURTHER_EVIDENCE. No subtype has a measured boundary.

points.1_root_trust_anchor: An isolation boundary this user cannot reconfigure. The subtype is not chosen.
points.2_who_controls_the_anchor: Unknown. A same-user Docker daemon, WSL host path, or hypervisor session would not qualify.
points.3_how_created: Not created. Creation would be a later approval.
points.4_how_authenticated: Would require a measured identity of the boundary, not a path string.
points.5_how_retained: Inside the boundary, the existing handle-relative helper could run. That does not retain trust across export.
points.6_child_directories: Same FILE_CREATE design, on a filesystem the attacker cannot swap.
points.7_artifact_files: Same write_exclusive design, inside that filesystem.
points.8_artifact_verification: Reuse G.14.7 checks inside the boundary, then repeat them on the receiving side.
points.9_export: A single exit after the producer stops. The exit medium is unspecified.
points.10_export_destination: Must not be a user-writable path opened with CreateFileW, or the race returns.
points.11_receiver_provenance: Receiver recomputes hashes and records boundary identity. A hash is not source approval.
points.12_receiver_substitution: Unsolved until the import open is inside the same kind of boundary.
points.13_concurrent_modification: Unknown outside the guest. Inside, only as good as the guest filesystem.
points.14_crashes: A disposable guest can be discarded only if discard cannot touch production. Not set up.
points.15_cleanup: Discard the guest rather than deleting host trees. Not authorised.
points.16_partial_artifacts: Fail closed and do not publish a partial export.
points.17_hostile_metadata: Still requires the verifier and an approved source. Isolation does not review metadata.
points.18_same_user: Unknown. This is the property that would have to be tested before selection.
points.19_independently_verifiable: Nothing about a guest was verified in this stage.
points.20_assumption: Some future boundary exists and is not controlled by this user. That assumption is not evidence.

C.ineligibility: The model defines the demonstrated same-user attacker as trusted. The vulnerability remains.

points.1_root_trust_anchor: The operator's path, trusted by declaration.
points.2_who_controls_the_anchor: This user, including every process running as this user.
points.3_how_created: The current open_directory path. No new component.
points.4_how_authenticated: Not authenticated against an independent anchor.
points.5_how_retained: The handle is retained after open, as today.
points.8_artifact_verification: Current handle-read checks, which do not detect the pre-open swap.
points.10_export_destination: Declared trusted for the same reason, which is circular.
points.11_receiver_provenance: Would still need independent hashing, and would still lack directory intent.
points.12_receiver_substitution: Accepted if the substitute was written by the same user.
points.13_concurrent_modification: Post-open is contained. Pre-open is accepted.
points.17_hostile_metadata: Unchanged. The trust model does not review packages.
points.18_same_user: Treated as benign. G.14.8 showed that actor redirect an open.
points.19_independently_verifiable: The assumption is not independently verifiable. The attack is.
points.20_assumption: This user and every same-user process will not substitute the path for the whole download. Unsupported.
